Explore CWP datasets interactively

Source: R/explore.R
cwp_explore.Rd

Opens a Shiny application to filter one or several CWP datasets on the fly (for example on a species, a fishing fleet and/or a tRFMO) and see the result as time series, tables and maps. The totals are recomputed for every selection, so they are always exact. With several datasets, a tab shows the differences between two of them, by dimension and by cell (by default the first and the last one).

Usage

cwp_explore(..., filters = NULL, selected = list())

Arguments

...

The datasets to explore: data.frames, paths of step directories (as in Markdown/<step>) or paths of data files (.parquet, .rds, .csv). Name them to choose the names shown in the application, for example cwp_explore(init = "Markdown/rawdata", final = "Markdown/step5").

filters

Columns offered as filters. By default source_authority, species, fishing_fleet, gear_type and fishing_mode, when present.

selected

Values selected in the filters when the application opens, as a named list, for example list(source_authority = "IOTC"). A column listed here is offered as a filter even if it is not in filters.

Value

A Shiny application. Printing it (at the console) launches it; it can also be given to shiny::runApp().

Details

The reports stay the reference document of each processing step; this application is for looking at the data in more detail.

Examples

if (interactive() && requireNamespace("shiny", quietly = TRUE)) {
  cwp_explore(init = parameter_init_catch, final = parameter_final_catch)
}
